result.title: A gene informed benchmark for BioScoring of pathology foundation models
result.summary: Pathology foundation models are usually compared by their performance on downstream tasks such as classification and retrieval. While such benchmarks measure how useful a model is, they provide no insight into the biology it represents. We introduce BioScore, a benchmark that quantifies how well an image encoder captures cell identities, with spatial transcriptomics of the same tissue as the reference. A sparse autoencoder splits the encoder's patch embeddings into sparse features, which we cluster into a fixed number of groups. BioScore then measures, for each of 52 cell identities defined by marker genes, how specifically one group follows the identity's expression over the tissue. Because the autoencoder training is fully unsupervised, a match shows that the model represents the cell identity from the image alone. We score 8 pathology foundation models and 3 natural-image models. Every pathology model scores above every natural-image model (0.299--0.371 \vs 0.214--0.232), and paired tests separate three tiers among the pathology models. Unlike a supervised probe, BioScore needs no labels, builds its reference from the data and scores even from few sections, yet it ranks the encoders as a probe does. Its per-identity breakdown indicates which cell identities each encoder captures or misses.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 BioScore 基准：用稀疏自编码器把病理图像编码器的 patch embedding 分解为稀疏特征并聚类成固定组，以同组织空间转录组为参考，量化每组对 52 种 marker gene 定义细胞身份的表达特异性，从而无需标签地评估 8 个病理基础模型与 3 个自然图像模型表征了哪些生物学内容。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「稀疏特征分解＋聚类＋与外部参考做特异性对齐」的度量思路可供核查能否迁移到 LVR，用于判断 latent 状态是否保留任务相关的具体视觉证据；但原文只评编码器表征、不涉及推理与生成过程，迁移属推测。
